summary: All 12 runs successfully completed their assigned tasks with all tests passing. Every run followed an identical structural pattern: read test file, read source file, run initial tests, then iteratively fix bugs with verify-after-each-fix cycles. No run introduced new bugs through its edits, and all failure counts decreased monotonically. Runs fell into two groups by task complexity: 3-bug tasks required 20-21 steps with 4 test runs, while 2-bug tasks required 16-17 steps with 3 test runs. A subset of runs (6 of 12) included an explicit 'Pausing to consider' reflection message between fix attempts, adding exactly 1 step to their total compared to counterpart runs on the same task. This reflection consistently listed 4 numbered considerations but did not change the underlying fix strategy or improve diagnostic outcomes. All runs maintained perfect scope discipline, editing only the target module file within the specified task directory. The primary observable variation across runs was the presence or absence of the reflection step, with task complexity being the dominant factor in step count.
